question: The Commission presented a draft Directive on discontinuing seasonal changes of time in 2018. In March 2019, the European Parliament adopted its position on the proposal and voted in favour of abolishing summer time in 2021. Unfortunately, the Council has not yet adopted its position on the matter. The Council argues that an impact assessment of the Directive is needed before decisions can be taken, and several Member States have contacted the Commission and called for a detailed impact assessment. 1.
Has the Commission taken, or does it plan to take, action to carry out a detailed impact assessment of the Directive on discontinuing seasonal changes?
Has the Commission set a timeframe by which this impact assessment should be carried out?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (23.4.2024) The Commission did carry out an assessment on the basis of the substantial analytical evidence that already exists on the EU summertime arrangements. This was judged to provide adequate analytical support as regards seasonal time changes, which corresponds to the scope of the Commission’s proposal.

The result of this assessment was presented in the explanatory memorandum of the proposal for the Directive for discontinuing the seasonal changes of time1. Therefore, while there was no separate impact assessment, the Commission considers that sufficient evidence has been provided in line with the spirit of the Interinstitutional Agreement on Better Law-Making.

It should be noted that the choice of standard time was not covered in the Commission’s proposal, as this falls under Member States’ competence. It is up to each Member State to determine which standard time they would like to apply, taking account of possible scenarios for the choice of permanent standard time. The impact of this choice should therefore best be assessed at national level.
In light of this, the Commission does not plan any further assessment on this topic.
